Category description: It contains general information about the test campaign to which the specimen belongs.
Name: N
Definition: Number of test/specimen.

Name: N_id
Definition: Number assigned to the test/specimen. This number is used for naming the cuves files and figures. Normally, N and N_id should match, but if any test is deleted only N would be updated because it counts the number of tests/specimens included in the database. N_id remains unchanged because it is the notation to name the additional files (data and figures).

Name: Reference
Definition: Literature reference of the campaign.

Name: Institution
Definition: Institution that conducted the test.

Name: Year
Definition: Year of the document containing the test.

Name: Specimen name
Definition: Name of the test unit in the original reference.

Category description: It contains variables of the typology and geometry of the specimen.
Name: Unit type
Definition: HC (Hollow Clay), AAC (Autoclaved Aerated Concrete), CS (Calcium Silicate), LAC (Lightweight Aggregate Concrete), SB-C (Solid Brick Clay), SB-CS (Solid Brick Calcium Silicate), CB (Concrete Brick), HCB (Hollow Concrete Block).

Name: N° courses
Definition: Number of unit courses.

Name: H
Definition: Height of the specimen.

Name: L
Definition: Length of the specimen.

Name: t
Definition: Thickness of the specimen.

Name: Bed Joints
Definition: GP (General Purpose), TL (Thin Layer).

Name: Head Joints
Definition: F (Filled), TF (Thin Filled), MP (Mortar Pocket), UTG (Unfilled, Tongue and Groove), U (Unfilled).

Name: H/L
Definition: Aspect ratio.

Category description: It contains parameters to characterise the mechanical behaviour of each constituent material of the specimen.
Name: Void Ratio (min)
Definition: Percentage of voids reported. Minimum value of the range.

Name: Void Ratio (max)
Definition: Percentage of voids reported. Maximum value of the range.

Name: Unit density
Definition: Gross density of units (weight over the gross volume of the units).

Name: lb
Definition: Average length of the unit.

Name: wb
Definition: Average width of the unit.

Name: hb
Definition: Average height of the unit.

Name: fb,Ʇ
Definition: Mean compressive strength of units in the direction perpendicular to bed joint.

Name: fb,norm,Ʇ
Definition: Normalised compressive strength of units in the direction perpendicular to bed joint.

Name: fb,ǁ
Definition: Mean compressive strength of units in the direction parallel to bed joint.

Name: fb,norm,ǁ
Definition: Normalised compressive strength of units in the direction parallel to bed joint.

Name: Strength class
Definition: Mortar strength class reported in the test campaign.

Name: fmo
Definition: Mean compressive strength of mortar. When this parameter was not reported, the minimum value according to the strength class was considered.

Name: fm,c
Definition: Mean compressive strength of masonry.

Name: fm,t
Definition: Mean diagonal tensile strength of masonry.

Name: Emo
Definition: Elastic modulus of mortar.

Name: Gm
Definition: Shear modulus of masonry.

Name: Em
Definition: Elastic modulus of masonry.

Name: fv0
Definition: Initial shear strength of masonry.

Name: μ
Definition: Friction coefficient of masonry.

Category description: It contains the global conditions of the shear-compression test.
Name: Boundary conditions
Definition: Test boundary conditions reported in the test campaign: DF (Double fixed), C (Cantilever), O (Other).

Name: H0/H
Definition: Shear span ratio (ratio of height of zero moment to specimen height). When this value has not been provided, we have considered that "Cantilever" correspond to 1.0 and "Double fixed" to 0.5.

Name: σ0
Definition: Compressive axial stress (total axial load divided by gross cross section of the specimen).

Name: ALR
Definition: Axial load ratio (compressive axial stress divided by the mean compressive strength of the masonry).

Category description: It contains information about the global force-displacement response with characteristic values extracted directly from the full hysteresis
Name: F-d data
Definition: Availability of displacement vs force curve as data files.

Name: F-d figure
Definition: Availability of displacement vs force curve only as a figure from where it can be manually traced envelopes and bilinear curves.

Name: Env curve
Definition: Availability of envelope curve as data files. If either F-d data or F-d figure is "Yes", then the envelope can be obtained.

Name: Bil curve
Definition: Availability of bilinear idealisation curve as data files. If either F-d data or F-d figure is "Yes", then the bilinear idealisation can be obtained.

Name: Failure mode
Definition: S (Shear), F (Flexure), H- (Hybrid followed by two main mechanisms), G (gaping), SL (Sliding), D (uncertain).

Name: δcr
Definition: Drift at onset of cracking (drift at first crack reported in the test).

Name: δVmax+
Definition: Drift at maximum shear force in the positive direction.

Name: δVmax-
Definition: Drift at maximum shear force in the negative direction.

Name: Vmax+
Definition: Maximum shear force in the positive direction.

Name: Vmax-
Definition: Maximum shear force in the negative direction.

Name: δmax+
Definition: Maximum drift recorded under controlled conditions (before collapse) in the positive direction.

Name: δmax-
Definition: Maximum drift recorded under controlled conditions (before collapse) in the negative direction.

Name: Vδmax+
Definition: Shear force at maximum drift recorded under controlled conditions (before collapse) in the positive direction.

Name: Vδmax-
Definition: Shear force at maximum drift recorded under controlled conditions (before collapse) in the negative direction.

Category description: It contains the variables to characterise the bilinear idealisation following Pavia approach. Depending on the number of cycles of the loading protocol, envelopes for each cycle are determined in the positive and negative direction.
Name: Vbil+
Definition: Equivalent shear force of the bilinear curve's plateau in the positive direction. This corresponds to the mean value of each shear force of the cyclic bilinear curve's plateau in the positive direction. The shear force of the cyclic bilinear curve's plateau in the positive direction (horizontal branch), determined by ensuring that the areas below the positive cyclic envelope curve and below the equivalent bilinear curve are equal.

Name: Vbil-
Definition: Equivalent shear force of the bilinear curve's plateau in the negative direction. This corresponds to the mean value of each shear force of the cyclic bilinear curve's plateau in the negative direction. The shear force of the cyclic bilinear curve's plateau in the negative direction (horizontal branch), determined by ensuring that the areas below the negative cyclic envelope curve and below the equivalent bilinear curve are equal.

Name: δe+
Definition: Equivalent yielding drift in th positive direction. This corresponds to the mean value of each cyclic yielding drift in the positive direction. The  cyclic yielding drift in the positive direction is determined by intersecting the two branches of the positive cyclic envelope.

Name: δe-
Definition: Equivalent yielding drift in th negative direction. This corresponds to the mean value of each cyclic yielding drift in the negative direction. The  cyclic yielding drift in the negative direction is determined by intersecting the two branches of the negative cyclic envelope.

Name: δu+
Definition: Equivalent ultimate drift in the positive direction. This corresponds to the minimum value of each cyclic ultimate drift in the positive direction. The cyclic ultimate drift in the positive direction is the drift obtained  at 20% drop of positive maximum shear force in the positive cyclic envelope.

Name: δu-
Definition: Equivalent ultimate drift in the negative direction. This corresponds to the minimum value of each cyclic ultimate drift in the negative direction. The cyclic ultimate drift in the negative direction is the drift obtained  at 20% drop of negative maximum shear force in the negative cyclic envelope.

Name: keff+
Definition: Equivalent effective stiffness in the positive direction. This corresponds to the ratio between the equivalent shear force of the bilinear curve's plateau and the equivalent yield drift in the positive direction.

Name: keff-
Definition: Equivalent effective stiffness in the negative direction. This corresponds to the ratio between the equivalent shear force of the bilinear curve's plateau and the equivalent yield drift in the negative direction.

Name: μu+
Definition: Ductility (equivalent ultimate drift-to-equivalent yielding drift ratio) in the positive direction.

Name: μu-
Definition: Ductility (equivalent ultimate drift-to-equivalent yielding drift ratio) in the negative direction.

Category description: It contains the variables to characterise the bilinear idealisation following Pavia approach. A single envelope is determined in the positive and negative direction considering the full F-d curve.
Name: Vbil+
Definition: Shear force of the bilinear curve's plateau in the positive direction (horizontal branch), determined by ensuring that the areas below the positive envelope curve and below the equivalent bilinear curve are equal.

Name: Vbil-
Definition: Shear force of the bilinear curve's plateau in the negative direction (horizontal branch), determined by ensuring that the areas below the negative envelope curve and below the equivalent bilinear curve are equal.

Name: δe+
Definition: Yielding drift in the positive direction, determined by intersecting the two branches of the positive envelope.

Name: δe-
Definition: Yielding drift in the negative direction, determined by intersecting the two branches of the negative envelope.

Name: δu+
Definition: Ultimate drift in the positive direction, equivalent to the drift where the positive envelope undergoes 20% drop of positive maximum shear force.

Name: δu-
Definition: Ultimate drift in the nagetive direction, equivalent to the drift where the negative envelope undergoes 20% drop of negative maximum shear force.

Name: keff+
Definition: Effective stiffness in the positive direction (secant to positive envelope at 70% of the positive maximum shear force). This slope determine the inclined branch of the positive envelope.

Name: keff-
Definition: Effective stiffness in the negative direction (secant to negative envelope at 70% of the negative maximum shear force). This slope determine the inclined branch of the negative envelope.

Name: μu+
Definition: Ductility (ultimate drift-to-yielding drift ratio) in the positive direction.

Name: μu-
Definition: Ductility (ultimate drift-to-yielding drift ratio) in the negative direction.

Category description: It says if any crack analysis was performed for this specimen and if yes, it specifies the method implemented.
Name: Crack measurements
Definition: Crack measurements reported, specifying the method used: No (if no crack measurements were conducted), method implemented/short description (DIC, deep learning, fractal, etc).
